issue_text: proveKind.Info() (prove.go:66-70) sets no NeedsJudge, so it defaults false, yet the prove executor DOES call an LLM judge in-process: symptomVeto (prove.go:359-382) invokes call(ctx, e.symptom, ...) on every Proven reproduction/deletion, and call->callAs (kind.go:434-436) sets req.Model,req.Effort = in.Node.Model, in.Node.Effort — the prove NODE's own model/effort. Production wires Symptom: j (the run's judge) in cli/wiring.go:275, and the shipped workflow gives the prove node `model: $JUDGE, effort: $JUDGE_EFFORT` with the comment 'model/effort feed the reviewer's judge call' (workflows/sdlc-loop-proved.yaml:24). Because the machine gates Preflight on NeedsJudge (machine.go:101 at Init, machine.go:634 before Advance), the prove node's model/effort are NEVER validated by judge.Preflight (cli/wiring.go:294). A prove node configured with a bad model id or an unsupported effort therefore passes Init and Advance, and only aborts at runtime IF a reproduction/deletion happens to prove (surfaced via isReviewerConfigError, prove.go:374). A pins-only or all-survived prove run never surfaces the misconfiguration at all — the same misconfigured workflow passes some runs and aborts others depending on whether a reproduction proves.
why_real: This is the exact failure mode the sibling test's own comment articulates: TestKindInfoDeclaresWhichKindsCallAJudge (kind_test.go:1115-1136) states 'an LLM-calling kind that reports false is never validated: a bad model id or an unsupported effort reaches the run instead of failing at init' — then asserts Prove:false (kind_test.go:1135) with the FALSE justification 'prove ... calls a Prover (mutation engine), not a judge'. TestProveReviewerConfigErrorAborts (prove_test.go:640-650) proves a CodeJudgeModel error reaches the run and only aborts at symptom-veto time, confirming prove uses the node model for a live judge call. The machine contract (machine/types.go:107) says Preflight 'runs before Create for every judge-calling node (KindInfo.NeedsJudge)'; prove is a judge-calling node that declares itself not one, defeating init-time model/effort validation. Aligns with the recorded lesson 'a node that calls the judge needs model in the YAML or it's DOA in prod'.
tests_checked: kind_test.go:1121-1153 (TestKindInfoDeclaresWhichKindsCallAJudge — asserts Prove:false, comment claims prove does not call a judge); prove_test.go:434-504 (TestProveKindContract asserts info.NeedsJudge is false); prove_test.go:563-650 (symptom reviewer IS called with node identity; config error surfaces only at runtime); cli/wiring.go:275,293-294 (Symptom: j; Preflight = judge.Preflight(n.Model,n.Effort,...)); machine/machine.go:99-107,634-635 (Preflight gated on needsJudge); workflows/sdlc-loop-proved.yaml:24 (prove node carries model/effort feeding the reviewer). No test validates the prove node's model at init — this assignment is exactly what the sibling test warns goes unexercised.

issue_text: checkBugs (kind.go:214-232) validates b.Verdict against the `verdicts` set (kind.go:197), which accepts FIVE values: matched, real_but_ungold, hallucination, unverified_no_evidence, checked_but_unverified. But the rejection message (kind.go:224) reads 'verdict %q is not matched|real_but_ungold|hallucination' — listing only THREE of the five accepted verdicts. The two executor-minted verdicts (VerdictUnverifiedNoEvidence, VerdictCheckedButUnverified) that the adjudicate executor legitimately emits (kind.go:555, 568) and that a cmd delta may carry are accepted by the code but omitted from the user-facing 'valid options' text, so the message under-reports the valid set.
why_real: The `verdicts` map at kind.go:197 provably contains all five constants; the error string at kind.go:224 names only three. A user/agent whose cmd or adjudicate output uses checked_but_unverified passes validation but, on an unrelated bad verdict, would be told those valid verdicts are not permitted. It is a factual claim the code contradicts (category 4).
tests_checked: kind_test.go:166-266 (TestK1Decode) exercises only the 'maybe' invalid case (line 214) and never asserts the message body lists a complete/accurate verdict set; TestK6Cmd (kind_test.go:634-656) hits 'nope'. No test pins the enumerated list in the message, so the omission is unguarded.
